choices.text: All digestion happens in the mouth
Digestion does not end in the stomach: it continues in the small intestine, where most absorption happens.
Digestion ends when food is swallowed

questions.explanation: The trap claim is: Digestion finishes in the stomach. In fact Digestion does not end in the stomach: it continues in the small intestine, where most absorption happens. The stomach churns food and starts protein digestion, but enzymes in the small intestine finish breaking down all three nutrients and the villi absorb them.
questions.prompt: Which statement about digestion is correct?

questions.explanation: Each enzyme is specific: amylase breaks down starch, protease breaks down protein and lipase breaks down fat.
questions.prompt: Which pairing of enzyme and nutrient from scene 4 is correct?

questions.answer: About 370 kJ: fat releases about 37 kJ per gram, so 10 g releases about 370 kJ - more than twice the roughly 170 kJ from 10 g of carbohydrate at about 17 kJ per gram.
questions.explanation: Scene 2 gives the per-gram values: carbohydrate and protein about 17 kJ/g, fat about 37 kJ/g, so equal masses of fat carry over twice the energy.
questions.prompt: A snack contains 10 g of fat. Roughly how much energy does the fat alone release, and how does that compare with 10 g of carbohydrate?

questions.answer: The villi give the small intestine a huge surface area so digested nutrients can pass quickly into the blood.
questions.explanation: Scene 5 shows the villi absorbing the nutrients: their finger shape multiplies the absorbing surface of the gut wall.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain the job of the villi in the small intestine.

choices.text: Stomach - mouth - small intestine - large intestine - oesophagus
Mouth - oesophagus - stomach - small intestine - large intestine
Mouth - stomach - oesophagus - large intestine - small intestine
Oesophagus - mouth - stomach - large intestine - small intestine

questions.explanation: Scene 3 runs mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine - the stomach sits in the middle of the pipeline, not at its end.
questions.prompt: Which list gives the organs of the digestion pipeline in the order food passes through them, from scene 3?
